cohort: The study participants included 80 women experiencing postpartum haemorrhage out of 14,442 deliveries at a tertiary care centre, predominantly aged 25-30 years.
finding: Uterine atony was the predominant cause of PPH (64.86%), followed by traumatic PPH (27.02%), with previous caesarean section, multigravidity, placenta previa, anaemia, preeclampsia, and placental abruption identified as significant risk factors.
mod_finding: Previous caesarean section was identified as a significant risk factor for PPH, accounting for 25% of cases.
